newsitem.title: UK: Cleaner air to buoy UK demand for fertiliser.
newsitem.headline: Cleaner air to buoy UK demand for fertiliser.

text.p: Crop demand for sulphur across the UK will have to be satisfied by fertiliser because better air quality will mean less of it drops from the sky, delegates at a conference on "Fertilisers for Grassland" heard.

The warning was given by Dr Ian Richards, managing directpr of Levington Agriculture, speaking at the conference organised by the United Kingdom Agricultural Supply Trade Association (UKASTA) and the Potash Development Association (PDA).

In a copy of his remarks obtained on Thursday, he said fertiliser demand will rise as levels of aerial deposition of sulphur dioxide and trioxide decline because of a rundown of heavy industry and tighter emission controls.
UK farmers could expect to see a reduction in protein quality and yields across a range of crops including grassland.
"NPK or NPKS fertiliser grades are likely to become predominant for the second and third cut sileage crops," Richards said.
"Deficiencies in first cut are also likely in the next few years which will introduce the need for high N grade containing sulphur," he added.
Richards suggested that testing for sulphur could be included in the standard soil analysis.
